ai.description: The Central Asian cobra reaches 1.5–1.6 meters. It is yellowish to dark brown, often with faint crossbands. It lacks a hood mark and features distinctive subocular scales touching the eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Naja oxiana* lacks the distinct "spectacle" or "monocle" hood markings found on other Indian cobras, typically displaying a plain, unpatterned hood instead.
ai.habitat: The Central Asian cobra inhabits arid to semi-arid regions, including rocky foothills and scrublands, typically at altitudes ranging from sea level up to 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Central Asian cobra is primarily diurnal, often emerging during the day to hunt small mammals and birds across its arid, rocky habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Naja oxiana* is oviparous, typically laying 8–20 eggs in a clutch during the summer months (May–July) within underground burrows or hollows.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Naja oxiana* occurs in the extreme northwestern Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting the arid regions of Pakistan and high-altitude areas of the Hindu Kush.
